themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsor-, sovereign- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names off public markets, and the top end of the pipeline is still filling: Silver Lake is in talks to take Workday private at a ~$43bn market value (wday-silverlake-takeover-talks) and Thoma Bravo has signed a $4bn+ take-private of Accelerant barely a year after its NYSE listing (arx-thoma-bravo-take-private). Already signed: Bernhard Capital's $43-a-share deal for engineering consultancy Bowman (bwmn-bernhard-capital-takeover), Blackstone Infrastructure's Safe Harbor buying MarineMax at $53 a share (hzo-safe-harbor-acquisition), Nielsen's $13.60-a-share deal for DoubleVerify (dv-nielsen-acquisition), Apollo's firm 715p easyJet offer (ezj-apollo-takeover), KKR's $127-a-share agreement for Integer Holdings (itgr-kkr-takeover) and the completed $55bn PIF-Silver Lake-Affinity buyout of EA (ea-pif-consortium-take-private). Still unresolved: CVC and Veritas Capital are running competing GBP1.56bn proposals for Bodycote to a 2 September deadline (boy-cvc-takeover-bid, boy-veritas-takeover-bid), Grant Thornton and New Mountain Capital's $5bn deal for CBIZ runs a go-shop to August 27 (cbz-grant-thornton-acquisition), Pacific Equity Partners' SG Fleet vehicle bids A$3.60 a share for FleetPartners (fpr-sgfleet-takeover-bid), Trian is assembling co-investors behind a take-private of Wendy's (wen-trian-takeover-bid), InMode's special committee is free to act again now that the Haifa court has thrown out Steel Partners' injunction request (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), EQT keeps raising for Perpetual and keeps being rejected (ppt-eqt-takeover-bid), Curaleaf has gone straight to Aurora Cannabis shareholders with a US$4.00-a-share hostile bid (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid), and ADW Capital's $18-a-share proposal for Driven Brands was dismissed as lacking a credible basis (drvn-adw-capital-takeover-bid).

themes.label: UK-listed franchises broken up or taken private
themes.note: The London market keeps losing control of its own constituents to overseas and private capital, from the FTSE 100 down into the FTSE 250's industrials. Bodycote, the largest independent thermal-processing network in the West, has twin cash approaches a penny apart -- CVC at up to 915p (boy-cvc-takeover-bid) and Veritas Capital at up to 914p (boy-veritas-takeover-bid) -- with the board running both through confirmatory due diligence ahead of the 2 September Rule 2.6 deadline. Above them, Apollo's 715p-a-share, GBP5.7bn cash offer for easyJet is firm and board-recommended after Castlelake walked away (ezj-apollo-takeover), and Prologis has a recommended Rule 2.7 offer valuing Segro at ~GBP14.3bn that would remove one of the FTSE 100's largest REITs from the LSE (pld-sgro-takeover-bid).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the constraint has narrowed to energised power rather than plans for it. Core Scientific paid ~$444m to take ~440MW of in-service, grid-connected Oklahoma capacity off a rival miner and push its Muskogee campus toward 1.5GW of AI colocation (corz-polaris-acquisition), while Williams is paying up to $5.5bn for Momentum Midstream to connect Haynesville gas to Gulf Coast LNG and power demand (wmb-momentum-midstream-acquisition). How the build gets funded is the other half of the story -- including where the funding stops: Nvidia has cut its planned backstop for OpenAI's 10GW Pike County, Ohio campus to under $120bn from $250bn and will cover only the first phase (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), even as it signs MOUs with six of the largest private-capital pools to mobilise over $500bn of third-party financing for the same build-out (nvda-compute-financing-platforms). Intel is selling $15bn of new stock to fund fab capex (intc-equity-offering-2026) and Amazon's 2026 capex guide is up to ~$220bn with capacity constrained into 2027 (amzn-capex-raise-2026). On the equipment side Prysmian pays ~$3.8bn for Atkore's conduit and cable-management business (atkr-prysmian-acquisition) and Everus bought modular electrical specialist Epsilon Industries (ecg-epsilon-acquisition); at the silicon layer Sony and TSMC are putting JPY747bn into a Kumamoto image-sensor fab (sony-tsmc-image-sensor-jv), Doosan took control of Korea's sole wafer maker SK Siltron (doosan-sksiltron-acquisition), and Nvidia will co-design orbital compute payloads with SpaceX (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep being decided by courts and state regulators rather than at closing -- and this week the pattern sharpened into a pure courtroom problem. Paramount Skydance has now satisfied every regulatory condition in its Warner Bros. Discovery merger agreement, with Mexico's August 14 clearance completing 68 jurisdictions, yet it still cannot close until five days after a 12-day antitrust trial set for March 2, 2027, owing Warner holders ~$7m a day from September 30, 2026 in the meantime (psky-wbd-acquisition). Delaware's Chancery Court has voided Verisk's walk-away from its $2.35bn AccuLynx purchase, ordering it to try again while the FTC review that triggered the termination is still unfinished (vrsk-acculynx-acquisition). Western Union's Intermex deal cleared New York's DFS on August 14 only for California's DFPI to suspend its own approval extension the day before (imxi-westernunion-acquisition). The one roadblock that has come down is InMode's: the Haifa court denied Steel Partners' injunction request in its entirety, releasing the special committee to rule on the competing buyout bids (inmd-steel-partners-buyout).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding or locking in the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing and exclusivity remain the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, but the direct-exposure version is being trimmed while the syndicated version scales. Nvidia's six-firm compute-financing platforms are designed to lend against its own GPUs so labs, enterprises and clouds can afford to buy them, moving the credit risk to Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR rather than carrying it in-house (nvda-compute-financing-platforms) -- and on its own book Nvidia has cut the OpenAI Ohio backstop to under $120bn covering only the first phase, from $250bn covering the project (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop). The lock-in version continues alongside: SpaceX has committed exclusively to building its AI infrastructure on NVIDIA platforms, with the two co-designing orbital compute payloads (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership).
